speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources in light of plans for a large number of coal-fired and gas-fired Independent Power Producers in the region (a) how many of these projects is Singapore involved in; and (b) how can Singapore play a leading role in renewable energy financing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Investments into power projects in the region, as with other investments, are commercial decisions that businesses and financial institutions make to maximise their long-term risk-adjusted returns, amongst others.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Nonetheless, as the financial sector increasingly incorporates Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) considerations into their business decisions, we are witnessing a rechannelling of funds away from traditional projects to more sustainable ones, such as those involving cleaner renewables.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: My Ministry supports the financial sector in making this transition and works with the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) to promote the broader green financing initiative in Singapore, including increasing the financial sector’s awareness of environmental risks and opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: MAS works closely with the industry to provide guidance on managing ESG risks and support climate-related disclosures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The grant helps to offset the cost of obtaining an external review to ensure that the green bonds are aligned with internationally accepted standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: My Ministry will continue to work closely with all stakeholders to build on these efforts and develop Singapore’s competitive edge, not just in renewable energy financing, but across green financing.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Just a supplementary question following up from her answer.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I laud the efforts by the Government to boost the Green Bond Grant Scheme and the Sustainable Bond Grant Scheme, up to the amount of S$6 million.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I feel that the biggest problem in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), excluding Singapore, is the plan to increase in the coal-fired, gas-fired Independent Power Producers (IPPs).

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They are going to spew a lot of carbon into the atmosphere and the biggest problem is that renewables financing, in my view, is still slow in ASEAN.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State share if Singapore plans to enhance and relocate our investments into, for example, first loss funds in the region or renewable projects in ASEAN, together with other ASEAN countries possibly chipping in later on, rather than possibly investing in negative yield type bonds in developed markets?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: That, in some ways, could help to massively boost renewable projects in ASEAN and potentially reduce the greenhouse gases in ASEAN going forward.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: When we talk about financing of power projects, we must understand it in the context of the growing energy needs in the region, even as we move towards a low-carbon source of power generation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Investments into power projects, as with all other investments, are commercial decisions that the businesses and financial institutions will have to consider, taking into account, as I had said, maximising the long-term risk adjusted returns as well as other goals that they have.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It is an important governance principle that we adhere to.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But as I have said, the industry is becoming increasingly exposed to the risks and opportunities of the low carbon future.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, financial institutions are also increasingly incorporating the ESG goals in their positions, and I think that will lead to a shift of investment towards more sustainable activities.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: What we can do is for my Ministry to continue to support the financial sector in making this transition, working together with MAS, to promote more green financing in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As regards the specific question about investments, like into a first loss fund or renewable project, it is something the Member could discuss and bring up at various forums for the investors and the financial institutions to consider the feasibility, not just in Singapore but across the region.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But they have said that sustainability is one of the factors that they take into account in their decisions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said earlier, the Government does not interfere or influence the decisions that they make on a commercial basis and this is an important principle of governance that we adhere to.
